title: WRAP Selected by WOFT to Support Florida’s $475,000 Teacher Safety Training Initiative
summary: WOFT and WRAP will jointly support the state-funded initiative, extending WRAP’s early-intervention, situational-awareness and force-avoidance training principles beyond law enforcement and creating a model for broader professional safety markets MIAMI, Aug.
body_text: WRAP Selected by WOFT to Support Florida’s $475,000 Teacher Safety Training Initiative August 14, 2026 PDF Version WOFT and WRAP will jointly support the state-funded initiative, extending WRAP’s early-intervention, situational-awareness and force-avoidance training principles beyond law enforcement and creating a model for broader professional safety markets MIAMI, Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Wrap Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: WRAP) (“WRAP” or the “Company”), a global public safety technology and training company, today announced that it has been selected by WOFT Charities (“WOFT”) to support training services associated with the WOFT (Where Our Families Train) Teacher Safety Training Program , which has been awarded $475,000 in Florida’s Fiscal Year 2026–27 state budget . The appropriation appears in the Conference Report for HB 5001E as “WOFT: Teacher Safety Training Program (HF 1031) (SF 1890)” in the amount of $475,000. The initiative will provide practical safety and preparedness training for teachers, administrators and other school personnel. WOFT has selected WRAP to support the effort with training methodologies centered on situational awareness, threat recognition, early intervention, de-escalation and avoiding physical confrontation whenever possible . For WRAP, the engagement extends principles the Company teaches within law enforcement into a broader professional safety environment: awareness comes first, and the best physical confrontation is often the one recognized early enough to avoid. “Everything starts with awareness,” said Jared Novick, President of WRAP . “That is true for a law enforcement officer responding to a call, and it is equally relevant to a teacher responsible for a classroom. Recognizing threat indicators, understanding when circumstances are changing, and knowing how to avoid or de-escalate a confrontation are foundational skills. WOFT laid the groundwork to bring those principles into Florida schools, and we are excited to support them in delivering it.” The program closely aligns with WRAP’s training philosophy. WOFT’s underlying proposal calls for mindset and situational-awareness instruction, hands-on real-world scenarios and dynamic group discussions designed to help participants recognize, avoid and de-escalate potential conflicts before they become physical confrontations . The $475,000 appropriation is made to WOFT, a 501(c)(3) organization, to fulfill the Teacher Safety Training Program. WRAP has been selected by WOFT to provide training support under the program and will receive a portion of the funding through WOFT based on the services WRAP provides. Accordingly, the full $475,000 appropriation should not be interpreted as an award directly to WRAP, nor should the entirety of the appropriation be interpreted as future revenue to WRAP. Training also includes practical self-defense, including the use of flashlights and pepper spray, with pre- and post-training assessments designed to measure participant knowledge and program effectiveness. Building an Integrated Training Model WRAP’s relationship with WOFT extends beyond this program. WRAP has exclusive access to WOFT’s training facility, which is becoming a national flagship environment for integrated WRAP training , bringing together instructors, methodologies and technologies in realistic, scenario-based settings. WRAP draws upon trainers with subject-matter expertise from diverse law enforcement, public safety and operational backgrounds. At the WOFT facility, those capabilities can be integrated into real-world scenarios requiring participants to recognize changing conditions, identify threat indicators, make decisions under pressure and determine an appropriate response. “Real-world scenario training should not be limited to law enforcement,” Novick continued. “Whether you are a police officer, member of the military, teacher, security professional or private citizen, the foundation is awareness. The scenarios and appropriate responses may be very different, but everyone benefits from learning to recognize risk earlier and make better decisions before circumstances escalate.” WOFT’s program framework provides for full- and part-time instructors, instructional safety equipment, personal protective equipment, mobile classroom capabilities and other resources necessary to deliver practical training. A Model Designed to Scale WRAP believes the Florida initiative demonstrates how training knowledge developed in public safety can be responsibly applied across education, private security, military and other professional safety environments, as well as private citizens . The common foundation is simple: recognize risk, understand what is happening, intervene early, when possible, avoid unnecessary escalation and respond appropriately when action becomes necessary. “WOFT created this opportunity, and our role is to help them deliver,” Novick said. “But we also see a larger model emerging. We can jointly serve law enforcement while applying the instructors, methodologies, infrastructure and technologies we have built to other environments where people are responsible for safety.” Over time, WRAP believes the model can extend beyond in-person instruction into a digital training ecosystem supporting continuous learning, recurring proficiency and certification . As WRAP’s technology portfolio evolves, the Company also sees opportunities to incorporate additional tools and technologies into the training environment, connecting what participants learn with how they perform in realistic scenarios. “We believe the future of training is integrated,” Novick added. “It is instructors, methodology, real-world scenarios, continuous digital learning and technology working together. WOFT gives us the physical environment to operationalize that model. Florida gives us an opportunity to demonstrate it with teachers, and we believe it can ultimately scale much further.” About Wrap Technologies Wrap Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: WRAP) is a global public safety technology and training company focused on developing tools, training and capabilities designed to support awareness, earlier intervention and more appropriate responses to challenging encounters. About WOFT Charities WOFT provides practical safety and preparedness training focused on situational awareness, confidence and real-world response skills. Through the WOFT Teacher Safety Training Program, WOFT will deliver training designed specifically for teachers, administrators and other school personnel. title: Why lenders should treat debit as a strategic payments rail
summary: Discover why lenders are prioritizing debit to reduce payment friction, improve delinquency outcomes, and create better borrower experiences.
body_text: A few years ago, I sat in a servicing center with a team trying to understand why some auto-loan borrowers kept drifting from 30 days past due to 60. The borrowers were not disappearing. Their ACH payments had failed, return notices surfaced days later, and by the time anyone followed up, the next due date was already approaching. That gap is where avoidable servicing work, borrower frustration, and deeper delinquency begin. That moment is why debit deserves a bigger role in consumer finance. Borrowers are making their preference clear: they want payment methods that feel immediate, visible, and easy to manage. Lenders that continue to default to ACH risk adding friction at the exact moment borrowers need certainty. The numbers don’t leave much room for debate According to the 2026 ACI Speedpay Pulse Report , 52.7% of consumers now use a debit card to pay bills, up from 42.1% in 2020 and a study high. Debit now leads credit cards (41.3%) by 11.4 percentage points, a margin nearly identical to the gap first recorded in 2018, confirming debit’s rise is a structural feature of how consumers pay, not a passing trend. New 2026 YouGov research commissioned by ACI Worldwide reinforces the shift: 53.7% of US adults now use debit to pay bills, more than any other payment method. The signal is especially relevant for consumer finance. The same YouGov research found that 16.1% of consumers already use debit for loan payments, including auto, student, mortgage, personal loans, and Buy Now Pay Later, with that figure climbing to 20.4% among Millennials. This is not a niche behavior. It is a broad shift in how borrowers manage money. The real problem: Billers stuck between two bad options Many consumer finance billers are caught in an uncomfortable middle ground. They are either bolting debit onto legacy platforms or working with providers that treat bill pay like retail commerce and miss the operational complexity of loan payments. The result is limited flexibility, avoidable servicing work, and payment experiences that do not match how borrowers increasingly want to pay. According to the 2026 ACI Speedpay Biller Impact Study , based on a May 2026 survey of 714 billers, only 18% are “very confident” their legacy bill pay platform will support future business objectives. That confidence gap helps explain why 76% plan to evaluate new bill pay options within the next 12 to 24 months. Tellingly, when billers do plan to invest, debit is where they are putting their money: 90% plan to add or expand debit over the next 12 to 24 months, the single largest planned payment method investment, and 66% already rate debit as “very important” to their bill pay strategy. Processing an ACH return costs $6 in labor. A debit decline costs just $0.10. Why debit outperforms ACH where it matters most for lenders ACH is familiar, and its per-transaction cost can look attractive on paper. But that headline number often obscures the true cost of ACH-based collections: returns, delayed failures, manual reprocessing, borrower follow-up, and compliance workflows. Borrowers do not see ACH as easier, either. In 2026 YouGov research, 37.2% said debit is the easiest payment method to set up for bills the first time, nearly double the 19% who chose ACH. That setup gap matters because enrollment friction is where failed payments and service costs can begin. Guaranteed funds and real-time validation With debit, authorization happens in real time. There is no waiting for a return notice days later and fewer reconciliation headaches. That matters in consumer finance, where payment timing affects interest calculations, late-fee logic, and regulatory reporting. Visa data shared with ACI in 2025 shows a stark difference when payments fail: the average labor cost of processing an ACH return is $6, compared with just $0.10 for a debit decline. Debit can also cut live-agent processing time in half, from eight minutes for ACH to four minutes for debit. Better delinquency outcomes Debit’s real-time authorization can help prevent the roll-forward effect that turns a 30-day past-due account into a 60- or 90-day problem. Visa data shared with ACI in 2025 shows that borrowers who use debit cards are less likely to miss payments, which can lead to up to a 20% reduction in delinquencies. Borrowers see the benefit too: when asked which payment method they trust most to help avoid late or missed payments, 30.6% chose debit, ahead of ACH and credit cards. Security that works in the background Security is another advantage debit brings to consumer finance, especially when it works in the background. According to the 2026 ACI Speedpay Pulse Report , 86.1% of consumers feel confident their financial data is secure when making bill payments, and consumers are layering on their own protections at a pace not seen in prior years: biometric authentication opt-in rose to 20.9% in 2025, up from 18.7%, and credit freezes jumped to 44.7%, up from 38%. In 2026 YouGov research, 41.6% of US adults viewed debit as more secure than other methods for large or recurring bill payments. The debit-plus-autopay convergence Debit and autopay are converging, and consumer finance billers that recognize this stand to capture meaningful value. 2026 ACI Speedpay Pulse Report data shows the number of consumers using both one-time and automated recurring payments grew from 43.4% in 2019 to 55.4% in 2025, while one-time-only payers dropped from 44.5% to 30.3%. In 2026 YouGov research, 47% of consumers said autopay or recurring payments setup would be the digital feature most likely to drive them to use debit for bills. That makes debit a natural fit for autopay. It settles against available funds, supports immediate confirmation, and gives borrowers more visibility into what leaves the account and when. Paired with reminders, tokenization, and flexible payment options, debit can help lenders create a more reliable “never miss a payment” experience. What borrowers are asking for Borrowers are not simply asking for another way to pay. They want payment experiences that are flexible, transparent, and easier to manage: 57.7% would use flexible due dates if offered 36.5% want automatic payments with reminders 30.4% want the ability to pause or delay during hardship Same-day payments behavior reinforces the point: 72.6% of debit users have already made a same-day payment on a bill or loan using their debit card. Borrowers often turn to debit when timing matters most. Making the economics work Debit has interchange, but ACH has hidden costs: returns, NSF fees, delayed failures, manual reprocessing, borrower follow-ups, and WSUD compliance workflows. When lenders account for the full cost of each rail, debit can be competitive or superior. Modern payments orchestration also gives billers more ways to manage card economics. Discounted network programs from Mastercard and Visa can help narrow the cost gap with ACH for recurring bill payment use cases, especially when paired with thoughtful adoption strategies. What this means for your payments strategy Consumer finance is at an inflection point. The 2026 ACI Speedpay Biller Impact Study points to the need for platform resiliency, expanded payment options, payments expertise, solution innovation, and industry focus. Debit sits at the intersection of those priorities because making it work well requires more than acceptance; it requires reliable orchestration, security without friction, and experiences built around the realities of lending and servicing. Here is what I would recommend to any consumer finance executive reading this: Design for every generation. Debit preference cuts across age groups, so the experience must work for mobile-first borrowers and those who still value familiar channels. The 2026 ACI Speedpay Pulse Report found debit usage at 74.7% among Gen Z and 64.6% among Millennials, while Boomers reached a study-high 31.0% in 2025, evidence that the runway for debit adoption is still growing across every generation. Make debit visible. Do not bury it behind ACH in the payments flow. If borrowers prefer debit, the experience should make it easy to choose. Design autopay around debit. Treat ACH as one option, not the default, and build recurring payment experiences around immediacy, confirmation, and control. Model the full cost of each rail. Look beyond transaction fees and include returns, service calls, reprocessing, and delinquency impact. Treat resiliency as a portfolio metric. Once borrowers rely on autopay, a platform outage can quickly become a delinquency event. The bottom line I still think about that servicing center and the borrowers who fell behind because the payments process itself got in the way. That is the problem debit can help solve. Debit is no longer a niche payment method. It is central to how consumers manage and move money. For consumer finance lenders, the opportunity is clear: make debit visible, reliable, and easy to use across every channel. In a debit-first world, success is not defined by whether a lender accepts the payment. It is defined by whether the payment works every time, across every channel, without creating effort or uncertainty for the borrower.

title: Slidesgo Reviews: Pros, Cons, & My Honest Take [2026]
summary: Slidesgo reviews are split, with 4.7/5 on G2 and 2.3/5 on Trustpilot. I tested Slidesgo and read dozens of reviews to see whether it's worth it in 2026.
body_text: August 12th, 2026 Slidesgo Reviews: Pros, Cons, & My Honest Take [2026] By Drew Hahn · 16 min read X LinkedIn Slidesgo has a template library people genuinely love and a public review page that reads like a warning label. On Trustpilot, it sits at 2.3 out of 5, labeled "Poor." So which is it? I spent time building decks with Slidesgo and read through dozens of user reviews to find out. The short version: the templates are good, but the subscription billing is where a lot of people run into trouble. Here's the honest picture on Slidesgo reviews in 2026, so you can decide whether it fits your needs. Slidesgo reviews: at a glance 🌐Platform ⭐Rating 📁 Reviews 🎯 What reviewers focus on G2 4.7/5 ~18 Template variety, ease of use, support quality Trustpilot 2.3/5 ~55 Billing, subscriptions, cancellation Business $19.99/seat/mo 1,000/seat/month Small teams needing a brand kit and collaboration Enterprise Custom Custom Larger orgs needing corporate branding and onboarding *Ratings correct as of August 2026. Verify with each platform. What this means: the template complaints are rare, but the billing complaints follow a pattern. Most trace back to canceling before the renewal date and getting charged anyway, which is the section worth reading closely if you're on the fence. What is Slidesgo? Slidesgo is a Google Slides and PowerPoint template library . You browse templates by topic, style, and color, then open them directly in Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Canva. It also includes an AI Presentation Maker , which drafts an editable deck once you describe a topic and pick a theme. Every template gives you a finished layout to start from, so you skip the blank slide and start editing right away. Key Slidesgo features Slidesgo has grown well past a plain template downloader, and most of what makes it useful shows up once you start editing. Here's what the platform offers: Template library: Browse a large library of presentation templates for business, education, and creative use cases. AI Presentation Maker: Enter a topic and choose a style, and Slidesgo generates an editable deck using hundreds of template designs. Extensive customization: You can change colors, fonts, images, and layouts on most templates, while some design elements are controlled from the master slides. Built-in visual assets: Slidesgo includes access to icons and other design resources, including Flaticon content, to make it easier to update visuals while editing. Data visualization: Slidesgo templates include editable charts, infographics, and other visual elements you can update with your own data. Multi-format export: Many Slidesgo templates are available for Google Slides or PowerPoint, and selected templates can also be opened in Canva. Free and Premium access: Registered free users get 3 template downloads a month and must keep the attribution slide, while Premium removes attribution and raises downloads up to 150 per month. Slidesgo reviews: what real users say I reviewed recent feedback on G2 and Trustpilot , along with a couple of expert reviews, to see what people experience with Slidesgo. Review volume on the newer AI features is still thin , so what follows blends that limited feedback with my own hands-on testing. Overall, I found that users appreciate the template quality and how fast they can get a deck done, though reviews consistently point to billing and cancellation problems as the platform grows. Here's what users and reviewers have shared about their Slidesgo experience: Pros Fast AI-to-design conversion: A reviewer said Slidesgo's prompt-to-design conversion runs fast and produces reliable output, with slides they could rewrite as needed. Reliable free templates: The free plan gives you access to a rotating set of ready-to-use designs, no payment details required to start. Broad format compatibility: Fritz.ai's hands-on review confirmed templates work across Google Slides, PowerPoint, and Canva without conversion issues, so switching tools mid-project doesn't break the file. Consistent design within a deck: Reviewers note that fonts and colors stay matched across slides, so a single template can deliver 20 or more usable layouts without extra tweaking. Speed from blank tab to usable deck: Kroma.ai's testing found you can search, click download, and start editing a working file within minutes, no account setup required first. Cons Templates aren't unique: Reviewers note the same designs show up repeatedly in classrooms and online, which can undercut originality for brand work. Google Slides formatting bugs: Fonts not rendering, charts losing formatting on import, and slide-master edits not sticking are recurring technical complaints in hands-on testing. Attribution restricts commercial use: Kroma.ai's review found the free-plan attribution requirement risky for client-facing decks, since it signals an off-the-shelf template to stakeholders. Missing polish features: Reviewers also point to a few gaps, like the lack of animation options, limited file format support for conversions, and no way to track task history. The billing and cancellation complaints (and how to cancel Slidesgo) The single loudest theme in Slidesgo reviews is money. Users report being charged after canceling and still getting invoices for months. A few describe a 500 error inside the "My Subscription" menu that blocks cancellation outright. I can't verify every individual charge, but the pattern is too consistent to wave off. So if you subscribe, protect yourself. Here’s what to keep in mind: ⚠️ Problem ✅ What to do Auto-renew surprises you Cancel before your renewal date, once 24 hours have passed since your last payment. There's no separate auto-renew toggle (canceling is what stops the renewal). Cancellation won't go through Cancel under account > My Subscription, then screenshot the confirmation screen You're still getting invoices Email support with a clear subject line and your account email, and keep every reply Charges keep coming anyway Dispute through your card issuer; EU users can cite consumer-protection rights Per Slidesgo's own FAQ , you can request a refund within 30 days of payment if you haven't downloaded any template. Once you cancel, you keep Premium access through the end of your paid period, but Slidesgo doesn't refund the unused portion. 💡 Tip: If you aren’t sold on Slidesgo, consider Gamma or another AI presentation maker . Is Slidesgo safe, or is it a scam? Slidesgo is not a scam. It's a legitimate product from Freepik, a well-established design company, and millions of people use its templates without incident. The real risk is the subscription itself: the billing and cancellation complaints are documented and repeated, and there are scattered reports of spam email and data-handling gripes. Fritz.ai puts it well - Slidesgo is legitimate, but the billing clarity needs serious work . Use it with the same caution you'd give any auto-renewing subscription. Use a disputable card, monthly billing, and a saved cancellation confirmation. My personal take on Slidesgo Slidesgo gets you a finished-looking deck fast, and that speed shows up the moment you open a template and start typing over the placeholder text. The template library does the heavy lifting a blank deck usually demands of you, and the design consistency held up better than I expected going in. Fonts, colors, and icon styles stay matched within a single template, so a 20-slide deck built from one design doesn't look stitched together from five different sources. Once I'd built more than a handful of decks, originality became the weak spot . I kept reaching for the same card shapes, and realized my "unique" deck probably looked familiar to anyone who'd sat through a class presentation or a startup pitch in the last year. The AI Presentation Maker carries the same trade-off. It earns its place as a starting point that saves you the blank-slide stall, but the content needs a rewrite before it's ready to show anyone, and the free plan's attribution slide is awkward to explain away on a client deck. The billing side is where my confidence dropped the most. I didn't personally get charged after canceling, but the pattern across reviews is consistent enough that I'd treat it as a real risk. Canceling early and screenshotting the confirmation isn't optional advice here, it's a precaution worth taking. Here's my verdict: Slidesgo earns its keep for teachers, students, and anyone who needs a clean deck fast and doesn't mind a template someone else has probably used too. If you're billing a client for the work or building something that needs to look unmistakably yours, budget extra time to rework the design, and keep a close eye on your subscription from day one. Is Slidesgo right for you? After testing decks in Slidesgo and reading through what reviewers experienced, I found it fits some situations well and falls apart in others. Here's how to tell if it fits your situation: Who will love it Teachers and students: Lesson slides and class projects don't need brand control, so a fast, good-looking template covers most of what you need. Anyone drafting internally: Team updates, brainstorms, and workshop decks rarely get scrutinized for originality, which is exactly where Slidesgo's speed pays off. Founders sketching a first pitch: The AI Presentation Maker and pitch templates get a rough idea into deck form fast, something to refine later, not present tomorrow. Occasional deck builders: If you only need a presentation a few times a month, the 3 free downloads and rotating template selection rarely get in your way. Anyone who wants Google Slides and PowerPoint flexibility: Templates open cleanly in both, plus Canva, so you're not locked into one tool. Who should avoid it Agencies and freelance designers: Client-facing decks need to look yours , and a stakeholder who's seen a Slidesgo template before will recognize it. Brand-strict teams: Fonts, colors, and layouts don't always bend to match brand guidelines, and there's no system in place to enforce consistency across a team. Anyone billing for polished, original design: The same layouts get reused often enough that a "unique" deck can end up looking familiar to your audience. Frequent downloaders: The free plan caps out fast, and heavy monthly use pushes you toward a paid tier and its billing complaints. Anyone wary of subscription cancellation issues: If canceling and confirming it stuck matters to you, go in prepared to screenshot everything and monitor your card statement. The best Slidesgo alternative for data-driven decks: Julius Slidesgo reviews praise the template library for speed and design polish, but that praise sits at the slide level. If your presentation starts with a spreadsheet, a set of financial figures, or a question you haven't answered yet, Slidesgo gives you a good-looking shell with nothing inside it, and the analysis still has to happen somewhere else first. Julius is a data analysis tool with its own presentation maker built in. We designed it so the same tool that works through your numbers can also turn them into a deck, no separate design app required. Here's what you can do with Julius: Start from a question instead of a spreadsheet: Ask Julius directly and skip the file upload. It can connect your own sources, search the web for public data, or pull institutional-grade financials on more than 17,000 companies through the Financial Datasets integration . Carry your analysis straight into a deck: Once you build a chart or a report in Julius, that same output flows into the AI presentation maker without a rebuild, so a finished analysis becomes a finished slide. Get sharper answers as you connect more data: Julius's Learning Sub Agent studies how your tables and columns relate every time you connect a new source, so it can find the right numbers faster on each question after your first. Data privacy and security : Julius holds GDPR, SOC 2 Type II, and TX-RAMP compliance. Your data stays encrypted in transit and at rest, is never shared between customers, and is never used to train AI models. If you want the analysis and the deck handled by one tool, try Julius for free today . Frequently asked questions Is Slidesgo free? Yes, Slidesgo is free with limits . Registering gets you 3 template downloads a month with an attribution slide and limited AI access. A Premium subscription raises your download limit to 150 templates a month and removes the attribution slide. Is Slidesgo safe to use? Yes, Slidesgo is safe to use . It's a legitimate product from Freepik, a well-known design resource company. The main risk is subscription billing, so pay monthly and keep a cancellation record. How do I cancel a Slidesgo subscription? Cancel a Slidesgo subscription from your account under "My Subscription," then screenshot the confirmation. If invoices keep coming, email support with your account email, and dispute the charge through your card issuer as a last resort. Can you use Slidesgo templates for commercial work? Yes, you can use Slidesgo templates for commercial work, but free-tier downloads require keeping the Slidesgo attribution slide , which many clients won't accept. Premium removes the attribution requirement, though you should check current license terms before final use. Is Slidesgo worth it? Yes, Slidesgo is worth it for teachers, students, and quick internal decks , since it saves time without requiring design skill. It's a weaker fit for client or agency work, where the attribution requirement and overused templates work against you.

title: Introducing the Newsroom’s Motion Graphics Team
summary: I’m excited to announce our Motion Graphics unit, a growing team that is already elevating how we use animated graphics and motion design and in our video journalism. Working in close collaboration…
body_text: Ana Simões joins The Times as team editor, and James Surdam and Stephanie Swart take on new roles. Read more below from Deputy Managing Editor Steve Duenes. I’m excited to announce our Motion Graphics unit, a growing team that is already elevating how we use animated graphics and motion design and in our video journalism. Working in close collaboration with Video, Digital News Design and Graphics, the team responds to the demands of all kinds of stories and formats, pursuing everything from news explainers and visual investigations to enterprise series and shows. Ana Simões started in June, and she leads this group as Motion Graphics editor. She joined us from Apple, where she was on Apple Music’s content design team, developing campaigns and digital products. Before that, she was the creative director for design and graphics at Vice News, leading a team of designers developing motion graphics, visual identities, and information design systems for documentaries, nightly news programming, and digital reporting. While at Vice, Ana won an Emmy for Outstanding Design and Art Direction for News. After moving to New York 10 years ago, Ana spent several years working across branding and graphic design projects. Originally from Portugal, where she earned her master’s degree in editorial design, she began her career in design studios focused on books, posters, and cultural branding. Photo Credit: Earl Wilson James Surdam has been promoted to assistant editor, Motion Graphics, and will be a key partner to Ana on visual direction and systems. This promotion recognizes James’s exceptional role in driving excellent motion graphics for our videos. James became an art director for Social Visuals three years ago, innovating on formats and providing direction for breaking news, enterprise and social packages. He helped grow the newsroom’s motion graphics staff, and he developed new approaches — and his work was critical to last year’s rollout of the Watch tab. He has mentored colleagues and strengthened visual standards by building design systems that have improved how our journalism is expressed on and off platform. James worked on a series of videos on the Department of Government Efficiency, including Elon Musk’s cost-saving claims , the initiative’s big errors , DOGE’s false claims and its misreported savings , that won an Emmy. Mona Lalwani, a Video deputy, says, “As the art director on Reporter Video, James helped define how our journalism looks and feels in this new and ever-evolving format. He’s been a creative force across productions and a visual guide to many on the team. He operates with incredible kindness and generosity, even when he’s juggling multiple stories.” Prior to Social Visuals, James worked with Visual Investigations and Research and Development. Before that he was a motion graphics editor at NBC News, where he led a small team. James received his Bachelor of Arts in journalism and mass communication from George Washington University. Photo Credit: Earl Wilson Stephanie Swart has joined the Motion Graphics team as a full-time graphics and multimedia editor. Stephanie will continue to work with Video and create original designs and animations. Stephanie began working with the Digital News Design desk last year on a temporary assignment as a motion graphics editor, collaborating closely with Reporter Video. Since then, she has shaped the look of many culture, data and science stories, crafting complex visuals that have mapped the depths of Antarctica’s Thwaites glacier , taken viewers inside the Louvre jewelry heist , traced the workings of the New York City subway system and explained why your zodiac sign is out of date . Her work earned a gold medal from the Society for News Design, recognized for its “smart, precise execution.” More recently she has focused on urgent daily news videos, demonstrating strong editorial judgment and flexibility in a fast-paced environment. As Anna Casper, Reporter Video senior producer says, “Steph leaves a distinct and personal touch on everything she creates. Whether it’s iterating on and improving maps or thinking through templates that could improve future workflows, she greets every challenge with infectious enthusiasm and excellence.” Across it all, Stephanie sharpens the coverage and makes the work feel fresh. She is a thoughtful, collaborative problem solver who meets each challenge with creativity and care, all while bringing levity to the work and the team. Prior to The Times, Stephanie spent more than a decade as a freelance designer, creating motion graphics for Vox, Quanta magazine, The Wall Street Journal, TED, The Pudding and others. Her work has garnered several Emmy nominations. title: What Modern Fintechs Actually Need from Their Security Stack

Though frustrating, you might still be able to win back the customer. The stakes are often higher for fintech companies that rely on sensitive data and actual money moving around. If a payment API times out mid-checkout, or an account balance reads zero because a database query chokes under load, users might panic and assume their money is gone. Modern platforms need to catch credential stuffing, business logic abuse, and automated bots without creating deployment friction. When security modules integrate directly into CI/CD workflows, protection provisions automatically alongside app instances. title: JBS Reports Record Net Sales in the Second Quarter of 2026

body_text: Free Cash Flow was positive at US$130 million, improving by US$185 million compared with the second quarter of 2025 JBS reported record second-quarter net sales of US$23.9 billion, an increase of 14% compared with the prior year, reflecting strong performance across its diversified global protein platform. Adjusted EBITDA totaled US$1.257 billion, and profitability improved sequentially across most business units despite ongoing challenges in the U.S. beef sector. “We once again delivered record revenue, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio across geographies, proteins and brands. Despite varying market conditions around the world, our operating teams remained focused on execution, efficiency and disciplined capital allocation,” said Gilberto Tomazoni, Global CEO of JBS. Net leverage ended the quarter at 3.10x. JBS continues to maintain a strong liquidity position, with an average debt maturity exceeding 15 years and an average cost of debt of 5.7%. “We have a solid capital structure and adequate liquidity to navigate the different cycles of our businesses. Our focus remains on maximizing returns from investments already made,” said Guilherme Cavalcanti, Global CFO of JBS. Free Cash Flow was positive at US$130 million, improving by US$185 million compared with the second quarter of 2025. The improvement was driven by working capital management initiatives, including receivables discounting, export-related customer advances in Brazil and stronger accounts payable performance. Performance during the quarter reflected the benefits of JBS’s diversified operating platform, with strong results in poultry, pork and international operations helping offset continued pressure in the North American beef industry. Business Units JBS Beef North America reported record net sales of US$7.8 billion, up 14.2% from 2Q25, supported by historically high beef prices and resilient U.S. consumer demand. The increase in live cattle prices, however, outpaced the increase in beef prices, keeping industry spreads under pressure. The business reported Adjusted EBITDA of negative US$100 million, a significant improvement compared with the negative US$264 million reported in the same period of 2025. The business remained focused on operational efficiency, yield improvements and value maximization as industry cattle supplies continued to constrain margins. Pilgrim’s Pride reported net sales of US$4.6 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of US$360 million, with an EBITDA margin of 7.8%. Chicken demand remained firm across the United States, Europe and Mexico. In the U.S., profitability improved compared with the first quarter, supported by productivity gains, plant upgrades and greater efficiency in live operations. The Prepared Foods segment continued to deliver growth in both sales and margins, led by strong performance from the Just Bare brand. JBS Brazil delivered record net sales of US$4.6 billion, up 28% from 2Q25, and its highest-ever second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, totaling US$273 million, up 22.1% from the same period last year, despite a 12% increase in average live cattle prices. The business posted an EBITDA margin of 5.9%. Performance was driven by exports, with higher prices and volumes, supported by the Company’s market diversification strategy. In the domestic market, the business remained focused on key customers, expanding its portfolio of value-added products while strengthening commercial execution. Seara maintained an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 12.3%, supported by volume growth, operational efficiency and commercial expansion in both the domestic and international markets. Adjusted EBITDA totaled US$315 million. The business achieved net sales of US$2.5 billion, up 18.2% from the second quarter of 2025, and volumes exceeded 1 million metric tons during the quarter. Performance reflects higher capacity utilization, continued investments in automation and industrial efficiency, and the expansion of its value-added product portfolio. JBS USA Pork maintained profitability within its historical range despite softer domestic demand. Net sales totaled US$2.1 billion during the quarter, while Adjusted EBITDA increased 38% year over year to US$184 million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 8.9%. Results benefited from disciplined commercial execution, a favorable sales mix and continued growth in branded and value-added products, which help lessen exposure to commodity market volatility and support more consistent earnings across market cycles. JBS Australia generated 30% net sales growth compared with the second quarter of last year, reaching US$2.6 billion, supported by higher prices and volumes. The beef segment delivered solid performance across both the domestic and export markets, while the pork, prepared foods and salmon businesses contributed to a more diversified earnings profile. Adjusted EBITDA totaled US$218 million during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of 8.5%. “Looking ahead, we remain focused on improving operational performance, strengthening our branded portfolio and generating cash flow while maintaining the flexibility to navigate different market cycles,” concluded Tomazoni.

title: Into the Omniverse: How Open World Models Push the Frontier of Physical AI
summary: Open models, which anyone can download, inspect, modify and run on their own infrastructure, are what make that possible. Nowhere is that more crucial than in physical AI, where every deployment is a specialization problem.
body_text: Editor’s note: This post is part of Into the Omniverse , a series focused on how developers, 3D practitioners and enterprises can transform their workflows using the latest advancements in OpenUSD and NVIDIA Omniverse . In July, NVIDIA joined more than 200 companies and organizations in signing “ Open Weights and American AI Leadership ,” an open letter arguing that AI leadership will be measured not by any single frontier model but by whether an open ecosystem reaches every sector. Open models , which anyone can download, inspect, modify and run on their own infrastructure, are what make that possible. Nowhere is that more crucial than in physical AI , where every deployment is a specialization problem. Physical AI has to understand and predict consequences, not just appearances. To make this possible, w orld models learn how physical environments behave, what may happen next and which following actions make sense. They can generate physically grounded world and action data, simulate future states and provide a foundation that teams can specialize for a robot, autonomous vehicle or vision AI system. Open world models are already being used to generate training data, test policies and specialize physical AI systems. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 brings these capabilities together in an open model family, with leading benchmark results and adoption across robotics, autonomous vehicles and vision AI. And NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, part of NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, provides prebuilt capabilities for building simulation-ready worlds that physical AI teams can use to train, test and validate systems before real-world deployment. World Models Are the Foundation of Physical AI The data behind physical AI is difficult and expensive to collect at the scale required. Rare events and long-tail scenarios can be especially difficult to reproduce safely and repeatedly. World models enable: More useful data by learning physical relationships from large-scale multimodal scenarios. More diverse environments that vary in weather, lighting, objects and trajectories. A better foundation to build on and adapt to a particular robot, vehicle, sensor configuration, task or operating environment. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/cosmos-corp-blog-promo-1920x1080-1.mp4 A general model hasn’t seen a team’s particular robot, sensors or operating environment. Closing that gap requires access to model weights, a license that permits adaptation and the tools needed for post-training. NVIDIA Cosmos world foundation models are available under the Linux Foundation’s OpenMDW 1.1 license, enabling teams to post-train models on their own data and hardware. Specialization is where openness becomes a practical technical requirement. Specializing a model is only part of the workflow. Teams also need environments to generate data, run simulations and test behavior. Omniverse libraries help developers build simulation-ready environments, while OpenUSD provides the open framework for composing, reusing and exchanging complex 3D data across digital twins , simulations and synthetic data generation workflows. Together, Omniverse and OpenUSD cut the duplicated work that can otherwise pile up every time assets, sensor configurations or environmental conditions change. Cosmos 3: The Frontier Model NVIDIA Cosmos 3 — a frontier open physical AI foundation omni-model built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture — combines vision reasoning, world generation and action prediction, letting developers use one model family to understand scenes, generate synthetic data, simulate future states and build specialized world action models . Developers can use Cosmos 3 as a vision language model , as a physics-grounded world simulator that predicts future world states and generates large-scale synthetic data, or as the backbone for world action models, instead of assembling and maintaining a separate model for each capability. The family includes Cosmos 3 Super (64B) for high-fidelity world modeling, Cosmos 3 Nano (16B) for efficient reasoning and post-training, and Cosmos 3 Edge (4B) for on-device vision reasoning and robot policy deployment. Lightweight enough to run on edge GPUs, Cosmos 3 Edge can be deployed across NVIDIA RTX GPUs, NVIDIA DGX systems and NVIDIA Jetson, including Jetson Thor platforms. Across benchmark evaluations, Cosmos 3 ranks No. 1 on Artificial Analysis for open weights text-to-image and image-to-video generation, on PAI-Bench for world generation and in the image-to-video category of Physics-IQ . For robot policy, it ranks No. 1 on RoboLab . Cosmos 3 Super is also the highest-ranked open model on VANTAGE-Bench for vision understanding. In addition to Cosmos, NVIDIA’s physical AI stack includes Isaac GR00T for robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles and Metropolis for vision AI. How Developers Are Putting Cosmos 3 to Work Across industries, developers are building on NVIDIA Cosmos for physical AI applications: Doosan Robotics, LG Electronics, Samsung Electronics and Skild AI in robotics; Li Auto, Xiaomi and Afari in autonomous vehicles; and Centific , Fogsphere , Linker Vision , Milestone Systems and Yuan for vision AI agents powering industrial AI and smart spaces applications. The NVIDIA Cosmos Coalition extends this work by bringing together world model builders, AI developers and physical AI leaders to contribute models, research and evaluation methods. NVIDIA recently expanded the coalition to Japan , where robotics and manufacturing leaders intend to join and develop open world models for factories, logistics, agriculture, construction, healthcare and transportation. Together, these implementations and collaborations are establishing open world models as an adaptable foundation for physical AI across robots, autonomous vehicles and vision AI systems. title: A no-nonsense guide to video hosting for businesses
summary: Views tell you almost nothing. A guide to video hosting for business: where to host product and training video, and which engagement metrics actually matter.
body_text: Where should you host product and training video? There's no single right answer, because the answer depends on who's watching and what you need to prove. Start with the embed target and the audience, then let the analytics requirement break the tie. Here are the five options most teams actually choose between. A dedicated video host built for business, such as Wistia or Vimeo, gives you access controls, clean embeds, and engagement analytics down to the per-viewer level on higher tiers. This is the default for marketing and customer-education teams who care about drop-off and want video that doesn't drag their brand next to a competitor's ad. The cost climbs with bandwidth or seats, so it can get expensive at volume. YouTube is free, handles unlimited bandwidth, and its analytics are better than people expect: you get an audience-retention curve, average view duration, and traffic sources. The trade-offs are real, though. You can't gate access properly, unlisted isn't the same as private, and every embed is one recommendation away from pulling your viewer somewhere else. An LMS such as TalentLMS, Docebo, or your company's existing learning platform is the right home when training completion has to be tracked and attributed to a named learner. The video isn't the point here; the record of who completed it is — the input to any real time-to-competency measure. LMS-native video analytics are usually thin, but the platform ties viewing to a user, a course, and often a quiz score. Hosting inside the creation tool you already use to make the video removes a step. You record, edit, publish, and embed from one place, and you skip the export-upload-reconfigure loop every time content changes. Clueso works this way. You record a workflow , generate an AI voiceover and a matching step-by-step guide , then host and embed the video with basic view and drop-off analytics, without moving files into a separate host. The analytics are lighter than a dedicated host's, so pair it with an LMS when you need per-learner completion records. A general help center or CMS with a native video block (Zendesk, Intercom, or your docs platform) is fine for support content where the goal is deflection, not measurement — the video knowledge base pattern. You'll usually get play counts and little else, which is acceptable when the video sits beside a written guide that carries the detail. body_text: Intel-funded initiative expands education-to-career pathways across key U.S. semiconductor regions In this article: As the semiconductor industry continues to drive innovation across nearly every aspect of modern life, Intel is investing in the next generation of talent through the launch of the Semiconductor Education Pathways Program (SEPP) — a comprehensive workforce development initiative designed to strengthen education pathways from K-12 through post-secondary education and into semiconductor careers. SEPP is an Intel-funded program focused on building a stronger, more resilient semiconductor talent pipeline in regions that support Intel's U.S. manufacturing footprint. Through investments in students, educators, institutions and community partners, SEPP helps create opportunities for learners at every stage of the education journey while supporting America's long-term competitiveness in semiconductor manufacturing. Building the Workforce of Tomorrow The semiconductor industry relies on a highly skilled workforce spanning engineering, manufacturing, research, technician roles and emerging technology fields. Meeting future workforce needs requires collaboration across education, industry and government. SEPP brings together universities, community colleges, K-12 school systems and nonprofit organizations to create meaningful learning experiences, strengthen educational programs and increase awareness of careers in the semiconductor industry. The program supports five core areas: K-12 STEM and Career Technical Education (CTE) Student experiential learning opportunities Curriculum development Faculty development and educator training Graduate scholarships and fellowships By investing across the education continuum, Intel is helping students gain the knowledge, skills and hands-on experiences needed to pursue careers in microelectronics and semiconductor manufacturing. A Regional Approach to Workforce Development SEPP investments support programs across Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio and Oregon, states that play important roles in Intel's U.S. operations and the broader semiconductor ecosystem. The program's regional focus allows Intel to work closely with local educational institutions and community partners to address workforce needs unique to each area while creating scalable models that can benefit the broader industry. Examples of supported initiatives include: Undergraduate research experiences focused on semiconductors and microelectronics Faculty training programs in semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence and quantum computing Community college transfer and technician pathway programs Student design challenges and capstone projects Educator externships and industry immersion experiences Career-connected learning opportunities for K-12 students SEPP is one element of Intel's broader higher education portfolio that includes research collaborations and initiatives with U.S. National Science Foundation and the Semiconductor Research Corporation that reach community colleges and universities in over 32 U.S. states. Intel invests in K-12 education through a robust outreach portfolio that supports national nonprofits, school districts, and local organizations to strengthen learning opportunities for students and educators. More details on education programming can be found in Intel’s latest Corporate Responsibility Report . Creating Hands-On Learning Opportunities A key component of SEPP is expanding access to experiential learning opportunities that connect classroom instruction with real-world applications. Across participating states, students are engaging in research experiences, design challenges, earn and learn opportunities, boot camps and hands-on laboratory activities that provide valuable exposure to semiconductor technologies and careers. These experiences help students develop technical skills while building awareness of the wide range of opportunities available within the semiconductor industry—from research and design to manufacturing and advanced packaging. Supporting Educators and Institutions Educators play a critical role in preparing students for future careers. Through SEPP, Intel is investing in faculty and teacher development programs that help educators strengthen their understanding of semiconductor technologies and bring relevant content into classrooms. The program also supports curriculum development and collaboration among educational institutions to ensure learning pathways align with evolving industry needs. By equipping educators with new tools, resources and industry insights, SEPP helps create lasting impact that extends well beyond a single cohort of students. Investing in Long-Term Impact SEPP reflects Intel's ongoing commitment to workforce development and education. The program includes support for graduate scholarships and fellowships, higher education partnerships, student experiences, and K-12 initiatives. These investments are intended to strengthen workforce readiness, expand access to semiconductor education and help create sustainable talent pipelines for years to come. Working Together to Grow the Semiconductor Ecosystem Strengthening the semiconductor workforce requires collaboration across sectors. Through SEPP, Intel is working alongside educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, community partners and industry stakeholders to build pathways that help more students discover and pursue opportunities in microelectronics. As demand for semiconductor talent continues to grow, programs like SEPP play an important role in helping students, educators and communities participate in the future of technology and manufacturing. By investing in people today, Intel is helping create a workforce that will power tomorrow's innovations. body_text: An autonomous agent that runs end to end without human intervention, decides when to lean on its deterministic core for an exact, verifiable result, and when to bring a person in. All inside an open box that is auditable end to end. It is joined by MCP connectivity and a CLI for technical teams. San Francisco . Simetrik, the AI-powered financial operations control platform, introduces Simetrik Agent: an autonomous agent that executes financial control work end to end, in natural language and with no need for human intervention. It interprets the request, reviews the working environment, integrates the sources, identifies dependencies, and on its own configures, implements, reconciles, and analyzes exceptions. Agentic, with exact results when they matter. What sets Simetrik Agent apart from a generic agent is that it does not improvise where the business needs certainty. When a result must be exact, verifiable, and auditable, the agent turns to Simetrik’s deterministic core: more than 110 specific financial-control functions. The agent knows when to reason probabilistically and when to lean on that deterministic core, which always returns the same verifiable result. That combination is where Simetrik’s deep knowledge of the financial industry makes the difference: an agent that alternates probabilistic reasoning and its deterministic core according to what each task demands, with the governance guardrails needed to audit every step and prevent errors. This is how Simetrik becomes a natural part of the CFO tech stack. Autonomous and open box. It is not a black box, it is an open box. Unlike opaque AI, where no one knows for certain why it did what it did, with Simetrik Agent every decision is expressed in financial language any person understands, can supervise, and can change whenever they want. And the agent itself recognizes when a person’s involvement is key and asks for it. Far from slowing it down, that collaboration makes it more powerful. One control, three ways to operate it To extend that control beyond the platform, Simetrik adds two complementary paths. With Model Context Protocol (MCP), organizations connect the agents they already use, their own or built on models like Claude, Copilot, or Gemini, with Simetrik’s financial knowledge and control capabilities, without rebuilding reconciliation logic from scratch. And a command-line interface (CLI) lets technical teams create and run reconciliations, configure sources, automate exports, and integrate controls with CI/CD pipelines. Whether through the agent, MCP, or the CLI, everything runs on the same Simetrik capabilities and under a single standard of permissions, traceability, and financial control. “The future of financial control is agentic and autonomous. The difference lies in building an agent that truly understands the financial world: one that knows when a result must be exact and auditable, when it is worth bringing a person in, and that keeps everything visible so the team stays in control. That is Simetrik Agent”, says Santiago Gomez, Co-Founder and COO of Simetrik. Simetrik Agent, MCP, and CLI are now available to Simetrik customers. Learn more at simetrik.com . About Simetrik Simetrik is the AI-powered financial operations control platform. Its mission is to give finance teams the control to operate with speed, accuracy, and confidence in an increasingly complex environment. With an autonomous agent backed by a deterministic, auditable core, Simetrik automates complex reconciliations and end-to-end financial controls, and provides a single source of truth over which people retain full control. Today, more than 180 leading companies across 50+ countries trust Simetrik to process 2.5 billion daily records, cut losses, and accelerate growth.
